NEAR mainnet13 Feb – 12 Nov 2026901 epochs

NEAR gives back 12.0% of what it mints. Break-even is 8.4× away, not 108×.

⏱Short on time? Read it in 60 secondsOne idea per step, in plain words→

NEAR mints about 2.5% of its supply a year. A fee-burn dashboard sees only the gas burn, 0.92% of issuance, and puts break-even 108 times away. Since April 2026 the NEAR Intents contract has also been sending NEAR to a buyback account, where it is held, not burnt. Count that, and burn plus buybacks offset 12.0% of issuance.1

Headline window: last 100 epochs, 29 days, ending 2026-11-12 20:50 UTC. Every figure rebuilds offline with one command and a result hash.6

Verdict for an investor
  • TodayNot yet a supply story. NEAR still mints about 8× what it wins back, and at the median growth rate in the data break-even is in 2091. Don't own NEAR expecting buybacks to offset dilution soon.
  • The betGovernance, not growth. Sending every Intents fee to the buyback (today about 23%) and HSP-029's lower issuance would bring even the base case to about 8 years. Both are votes, not market conditions.
  • Turn more bullish ifHSP-029 clears its veto window (closes 16 Nov 2026), and validators adopt it after the 90-day grace period, or the buyback's share of Intents fees rises toward 50%.
  • Turn bearish ifthe buyback balance keeps falling, payback over 100 epochs drops below 6%, or transfers stop coming from intents.near.

01The claim

Burn and buybacks offset an eighth of issuance. A burn-only view sees a hundredth.

Payback is burn plus the buyback account's gain, divided by NEAR minted to validators. Mint and burn come from total_supply in block headers, exact to the yoctoNEAR; the buyback gain is a balance change between epoch ends.2

03The models

Three levers move payback. Two of them are governance votes.

Payback scales with Intents volume and with the share of gross Intents fees reaching the buyback account, and inversely with the issuance rate. HSP-029, passed by NEAR's House of Stake on 2 November 2026 and awaiting ratification, would lower maximum issuance to 1.6% a year.5

04The path to break-even

Break-even turns on growth and capture. At Intents' volume trend it comes in about 5 years; at slow growth, capturing every Intents fee with HSP-029 brings it to 8.

Not a forecast: three growth rates taken from the data by one rule, and where each takes payback from today's 12.0%. HSP-029, passed on 2 November 2026 and awaiting ratification, moves every date earlier; it does not change which paths arrive.8

Bear · −25.5% a year
Never

never with HSP-029 either

If gross Intents fees keep shrinking as they did over the past year, the flow shrinks with them and never reaches issuance.

Base · +3.4% a year
2091in 64 years

2077 with HSP-029 (51 years)

At the median year-long rate, payback is 17% of issuance in ten years. At this pace, growth alone is too slow; capture is the lever.

Bull · +50.2% a year
2032in 5 years

2031 with HSP-029 (4 years)

If Intents volume keeps the trend it set over the past year, break-even comes in about 5 years. Five-year break-even needs 53% a year.

Issuance

Today's flow would equal issuance if issuance were 0.30% a year. HSP-029's 1.6% takes the distance from 8.4× to 5.3×. Capture is the larger lever: all of it, with HSP-029, brings the base case to 8 years.

How the three rates are set: one rule, not a choice. The captured flow is nine months old and was ramping up, so its own growth is not used; what drives it is (buybacks are 92% of payback and follow NEAR Intents volume, r = 0.90 by week). Four year-long rates from the DefiLlama year: Intents volume, last 30 days against the first 30 (+1.9%) and log-linear trend (+50.2%); gross Intents fees, the same two ways (−25.5%, +4.8%). Bear is the lowest, base the median, bull the highest. Shorter windows are left out: they annualise August's jump into several hundred percent a year. Paths start at today's 12.0% and hold capture share and NEAR price constant; HSP-029 is a linear ramp from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months, starting at its earliest possible date, 2027-02-14 (veto window closes 16 Nov 2026, then a 90-day grace period; validators must also adopt the upgrade). Dashed lines: with HSP-029. Shaded: between bear and bull. run.py: scenarios, scenarios in out/results.json.

05The case, both ways

The bear case gets the same page as the bull case.

Six points each side, at equal weight. The full argument, with what would change our mind, is in THESIS.md.

For

The flow is on chain, exact, and has levers.
i

The flow is on chain and exact.

9,922 NEAR a day reach the buyback account, against 829 burnt.

ii

It comes from one contract.

2,979 of 2,996 recent transfers were sent by intents.near.

iii

A separate pipeline agrees.

DefiLlama gives 13,589 NEAR a day for all revenue wallets; balances read from chain give 13,984.

iv

Capture is a lever.

The account receives about 23% of gross Intents fees. All of it, at today's volume, would be 49% of issuance.

v

Issuance is a lever in motion.

At 1.6% a year the multiple is 5.3× at today's flows.

vi

Intents grows as the chain shrinks.

intents.near's daily receipts grew 2.8× since February; its share of all receipts rose from 0.7% to 7.8% (BigQuery).

Against

Held is not burnt, and the trend matters.
i

Buybacks are not burns.

The NEAR sits in a multisig account. Supply does not fall and the holders can spend it.

ii

Payback has been falling.

From a peak of 16.5% on 19 September 2026 to 12.0%.

iii

NEAR Intents is not growing.

Over a year, daily volume is 1.02× and gross fees 0.75× (DefiLlama).

iv

The flow is concentrated.

One application supplies 92% of the payback.

v

The balance has fallen before.

10,283 NEAR left the account in 1 of 663 epochs.

vi

The chain got quieter.

Daily active accounts are down 70% and transactions down 80% since February. Most of the drop in app activity is one app, KaiChing, leaving (BigQuery).

“If the buybacks were burnt, net inflation would be 2.20% instead of 2.48%. They are not, yet.”Inflation if buybacks were burnt · out/results.json
06Network activity (BigQuery)

The chain got quieter; Intents did not. intents.near's daily receipts grew 2.8× while the chain's fell by 76%.

Daily active accounts, transactions and contract usage, from Google's public NEAR dataset bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us. Most of the fall in calls is one app leaving: over the first 30 days earn.kaiching and wallet.kaiching made 79% of all function calls, and neither is in the top 25 now. Daily active accounts fell in one step on 19 Feb 2026, from 504,588 to 146,971, which looks like a single exit rather than a slow drift. Over the same window intents.near's own activity grew in absolute terms, so its share rose from 0.7% to 7.8%: NEAR's activity is moving to the application that pays the buybacks. It does not by itself raise payback: the buyback account is paid from Intents fees, not from receipts.

How to run them

Open the BigQuery console (the sandbox is free and needs no card), paste a file from queries/, Run, then Save results → CSV (local file) as data/bq/<name>.csv. Or: bq query --use_legacy_sql=false --format=csv --max_rows=1000 < queries/x.sql > data/bq/x.csv. Then python3 run.py.

Kept apart from the result

run.py never reads these files, so the headline numbers and the result hash do not depend on an account with Google. Each CSV's sha256 is shown under its chart.

No Intents Explorer pull

The 1Click Swap API terms (section 4.1(e)) forbid keeping its data beyond 24 hours, so a committed copy could not be re-checked. Intents volume and fees come from DefiLlama's public series instead.

Notes & sources

How every number on this page was made.

The small numbers in the text link here. Each data file is hashed in data/sources.json, and test_run.py refuses to run if any of them changes.

  1. 01
    Headline window: last 100 epochs (29.3 days) ending 2026-11-12 20:50 UTC at height 224,265,136. Payback 0.119738; burn coverage 0.00922847; buyback coverage 0.11051. out/results.json → summary.
  2. 02
    Mint = supply(first) − supply(prev last) + burnt(first); burn = burnt(first) + supply(first) − supply(last), per epoch from block-header total_supply. data/epochs.csv.
  3. 03
    view_account balance of buybacks.multisignature.near at each epoch's last block, differenced (data/buybacks.csv). Senders from NearBlocks with transaction hashes (data/inflows.csv). A 505,041 NEAR transfer from another wallet is excluded as a lump (run.py: mark_lumps).
  4. 04
    DefiLlama summary/dexs/near-intents and fees/near-intents dailyHoldersRevenue, 37 weeks (data/llama.csv). Third-party context only.
  5. 05
    Lever model: payback = burn/mint × 2.5/i + buyback/mint × volume × capture/0.229 × 2.5/i, with i the issuance rate in % (today's maximum, 2.5%, from data/protocol.json). All Intents fees captured at today's volume gives 49.2%.
  6. 06
    python3 run.py prints RESULT sha256=50543274…09d1. test_run.py fails if any epoch of the buyback account is unexplained.
  7. 07
    predictions/, each round with an .ots proof: ots verify predictions/<file>.ots. Bands are 5–95% from window-to-window variation.
  8. 08
    Scenarios: run.py: scenarios and growth_measures; bear, base and bull are the lowest, median and highest of four year-long growth rates of NEAR Intents volume and gross fees (DefiLlama). HSP-029: gov.near.org thread, passed by the House of Stake on 2026-11-02 (99.96% of voting power, 36 voters). The Security Council veto window closes 2026-11-16 16:48 UTC; without a veto it is ratified, a 90-day grace period follows (earliest start about 2027-02-14), and validators must adopt a nearcore release. As of 2026-11-13 no veto and no release had been reported.
